description: Figure 3 (the first, top grouping) presents a set of three pie charts showing the distribution of problem outcomes by correctness under w/ KNOWLEDGE versus w/o KNOWLEDGE settings, split by difficulty level; there are three pies labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” and each pie contains four slices corresponding to the legend categories N+K+ (teal), N−K+ (yellow), N−K− (gray), and N+K− (orange). In the “easy” pie, the slices are approximately 61.5% (teal, N+K+), 34.6% (yellow, N−K+), 3.9% (gray, N−K−), and 0.0% (orange, N+K−). In the “medium” pie, the slices are about 65.4% (teal, N+K+), 30.8% (yellow, N−K+), 2.5% (gray, N−K−), and 1.3% (orange, N+K−). In the “hard” pie, the slices are about 39.6% (yellow, N−K+), 30.6% (gray, N−K−), 25.1% (teal, N+K+), and 4.7% (orange, N+K−). A legend with the four category labels and color swatches appears to the right of the pies, and percentage values are printed inside the slices; none of the slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized.
